thread:
taylor: quick sync — I'm prototyping a compatibility harness for new model ingests. want to discuss scope: cheap heuristics vs. full perf + quality sweeps.

devin: +1. can you sketch the two paths?

nisha: fwiw, we need something that fails fast in CI. long benches are fine async.

ryan: agree with nisha. primary concern is silent regressions in kv/cache behavior after quant/onnx conversions.

 taylor: cool. rough idea: two-stage pipeline. stage 1: smoke heuristics (fast, O(1) samples) — signature checks, tokenization parity, kv cache sanity, minimal perf numbers (latency p50 on tiny batch). stage 2: gated async bench — throughput, mem @ seq=1024, small eval suite for hallucination/quality.

devin: what are "signature checks"?

 taylor: name+shape+dtype for weights, presence of past_key/kv nodes, expected tokenizer special tokens. basically quick rejects.

bench-bot: automated note: existing validator takes ~90s on n1-small for a single model. aiming for <5s for stage1. :robot_face:

nisha: for stage1 we should run deterministic examples to catch tokenization mismatches. often happens with sentencepiece -> bpe shims.

ryan: also add a tiny kv-loop stress: feed same prompt 6x incremental tokens and assert logits continuity (no huge jumps). I can share a snippet.

devin: curious about thresholds. if a model fails stage1, is it rejected outright or flagged for manual review?

 taylor: proposal: stage1 failures -> automatic quarantine + short report (what failed). humans can triage and either whitelist with reason or reject. stage2 only runs for quarantined models after manual ok. keeps CI fast.

nisha: sounds reasonable. we should also capture quantization profiles in stage1 — e.g., run a tiny 8-bit sim and check output delta against fp16 for a couple of samples. if delta > X, mark as risky.

ryan: on the delta threshold: don't be overzealous. some model families shift numbers but behaviorally fine. maybe two signals: numeric delta and behavioral eval (intent-preserving on a 10-sample prompt set).

 taylor: agreed. numeric delta threshold = 1e-2 L2 norm on logits as a heuristic, but require behavioral mismatch to escalate. will document.

devin: how do we surface results? want consistent schema so infra+console can show pass/fail + artifacts link.

 taylor: will output a json report blob with keys: {compat_status, checks:[], artifacts:[log, kv-dump, mini-eval.json], durations}. sample schema:```json
{
  "compat_status": "quarantine",
  "checks": ["tok-parity","kv-loop-fail","quant-delta-high"],
  "artifacts": ["s3://bench/art-1748201123/log.txt"]
}
```

bench-bot: note: artifact retention cost warning if we keep full kv-dumps for every ingest. suggest ephemeral and keep only on failures.

nisha: retention policy: keep 7 days for pass artifacts, 90 days for failures. ok?

ryan: ok. on interface boundaries — let's make stage1 a single binary callable in both hosted and private pipelines. minimal deps (python + torch/transformers shim). stage2 can be a more heavy containerized job.

devin: question about onnx path: should we run an ONNX export in stage1? that adds time. maybe only run a light export check (exportable boolean) not full runtime comparison.

 taylor: yeah do a dry-run export for anomalies (missing ops) but skip runtime perf. if dry-run passes, mark onnx_exportable=true in report.

nisha: one more: can we add a policy for model families we auto-whitelist? e.g., internal fine-tuned variants of known bases. reduces noise.

 taylor: good idea. will add family_whitelist with patterns. humans can opt-in per org.

ryan: action items?

 taylor: I'll PR a PoC for stage1 harness (scripts + json schema) by EOD Thu. devin — can you draft the quarantine UI content? nisha — will define the mini-eval prompt set and delta thresholds. I'll open a follow-up thread for stage2 perf suite.

devin: on it.

nisha: will add prompt set + expected intents.

bench-bot: deploy note: new job template will be bench-stage1-quick v1. tagging CI for rollout after PR merge. :rocket:
summary: Discussion of a two-stage model compatibility harness: fast stage1 heuristics (signature, tokenization, kv loop, quick quant check) to quarantine problematic ingests, and heavier async stage2 benches for throughput and quality. Agreed on report schema, retention policy, whitelist option, and action items.
